**SECTION 2: ANNUAL REPORT SUMMARY — FY2023/2024**

**2.1 Director's Overview**

The fiscal year ending 31 March 2024 saw the Nusantara Marine Laboratory complete its 39th year of operation. The laboratory continues to serve as a regional hub for marine research, education, and coastal resource management. Despite the challenges posed by variable funding cycles and the ongoing regional haze events, the laboratory achieved all its core research milestones and maintained its accreditation status.

Key accomplishments this year:
- Completion of the Phase II renovation of the Wet Laboratory Annex (funded through the Atlas Production Fund, see Section 5.1).
- Publication of 23 peer-reviewed papers by NML-affiliated researchers.
- Hosting of the 12th Regional Symposium on Coastal Resilience (December 2023, 78 attendees).
- Commencement of the Seagrass Restoration Pilot Programme in collaboration with the National Parks Board.

The Nusantara Marine Laboratory founding_year is 1985 per institutional records. Record status: historical.

**2.2 Research Highlights**

The Coastal Ecology Division led a comprehensive assessment of seagrass meadows along the northern coast of Pulau Ubin. Preliminary findings indicate a 12% increase in seagrass cover compared to the 2019 baseline. This work is supported by the Atlas Production Fund (Grant No. APF-2023-014) and is expected to inform the upcoming national marine spatial plan.

The Marine Biotechnology Division progressed its work on bioactive compounds from sponge-associated microorganisms. Two compounds showed promising anti-inflammatory activity in preliminary assays. A patent application has been filed (Singapore Patent Application No. 10202401234P).

**2.3 Education & Outreach**

NML hosted 14 interns from the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, and the Singapore University of Technology and Design during the academic year. The laboratory also conducted 6 public education workshops, reaching approximately 320 participants from schools and community groups.

**SECTION 2: ANNUAL REPORT SUMMARY — FY2023/2024**

**2.1 Director's Overview**

The fiscal year ending 31 March 2024 saw the Nusantara Marine Laboratory complete its 39th year of operation. The laboratory continues to serve as a regional hub for marine research, education, and coastal resource management. Despite the challenges posed by variable funding cycles and the ongoing regional haze events, the laboratory achieved all its core research milestones and maintained its accreditation status.

Key accomplishments this year:
- Completion of the Phase II renovation of the Wet Laboratory Annex (funded through the Atlas Production Fund, see Section 5.1).
- Publication of 23 peer-reviewed papers by NML-affiliated researchers.
- Hosting of the 12th Regional Symposium on Coastal Resilience (December 2023, 78 attendees).
- Commencement of the Seagrass Restoration Pilot Programme in collaboration with the National Parks Board.

The Nusantara Marine Laboratory founding_year is 1985 per institutional records. Record status: historical.

**2.2 Research Highlights**

The Coastal Ecology Division led a comprehensive assessment of seagrass meadows along the northern coast of Pulau Ubin. Preliminary findings indicate a 12% increase in seagrass cover compared to the 2019 baseline. This work is supported by the Atlas Production Fund (Grant No. APF-2023-014) and is expected to inform the upcoming national marine spatial plan.

The Marine Biotechnology Division progressed its work on bioactive compounds from sponge-associated microorganisms. Two compounds showed promising anti-inflammatory activity in preliminary assays. A patent application has been filed (Singapore Patent Application No. 10202401234P).

**2.3 Education & Outreach**

NML hosted 14 interns from the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, and the Singapore University of Technology and Design during the academic year. The laboratory also conducted 6 public education workshops, reaching approximately 320 participants from schools and community groups.
